rearPatterns.title: Rear: cold middle — raise pressure
rearPatterns.why: A cold middle with hotter edges is an under-inflated rear. Raise pressure.

rearPatterns.title: Rear: hot middle — drop pressure
rearPatterns.why: A hot middle with cooler edges is an over-inflated rear. Drop pressure.

rearPatterns.title: Rear: hot inner — more transfer
rearPatterns.why: Hot inner, cooler outer means not enough rear transfer. Narrow the rear or stiffen the rear. Fix cone wear before the profile is ruined.

rearPatterns.title: Rear: hot outer — less transfer
rearPatterns.why: Hot outer means too much transfer. Widen the rear or soften the rear. Watch for hop.

frontPatterns.title: Front: hot inner — less negative camber
frontPatterns.why: Both front inners hottest usually means too much negative camber. If that also comes with turn-in oversteer, there is too much caster.

frontPatterns.title: Front: hot outer — more negative camber
frontPatterns.why: Hot outer, cool inner means the outside of the tread is working too hard. Add negative camber.

frontPatterns.title: Front: hot middle, even edges — drop pressure
frontPatterns.why: Camber looks OK; the tyre is over-inflated.

frontPatterns.title: Front: cold middle, hot edges — raise pressure
frontPatterns.why: Camber looks OK; the tyre is under-inflated.
